library_preparation_preflight.summary: micronaut-http-client-core only contains the HttpClient/HttpClientFactory abstractions and @Client annotation/interceptor/filter machinery; there is no bundled or transitive HttpClientFactory implementation, so HttpClient.create(...) throws IllegalStateException at runtime without a concrete client engine on the classpath, and @Client-based coverage needs the DI annotation processor to compile.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Tests should exercise both the imperative HttpClient/BlockingHttpClient path and, since the interceptor/annotation/bind/filter packages are the module's main added value, at least one declarative @Client interface plus an HTTP filter, resolved through ApplicationContext. Needs a real target endpoint: reuse a Micronaut EmbeddedServer (requires also adding io.micronaut:micronaut-http-server-netty as testImplementation if the driver doesn't already scaffold it) started on a random port (micronaut.server.port=-1), or fall back to a plain JDK com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer if avoiding another Micronaut module is preferred. No Docker image or environment/system property is needed beyond that.
risks: If the driver's normal scaffold for io.micronaut:* libraries already auto-adds micronaut-inject-java and/or a client implementation project-wide, the second dependency entry would be redundant (harmless but worth checking against the generator defaults).

Choosing micronaut-http-client (Netty) as the implementation is a test-time choice; io.micronaut:micronaut-http-client-jdk is an alternative concrete implementation and could be used instead if the driver prefers avoiding the Netty dependency chain.
